hero.intro: Meaningful products usually start the same way: a company realizes it is wasting time managing orders, customers, documents, scheduling, inventory, approvals, or task tracking.
hero.pullQuote: Sometimes, your company's next product is hiding inside a problem it already solved.

problema.heading: Every product starts with a problem
problema.intro: First comes the problem. Then comes the attempt to solve it.
problema.lead: A product doesn't start with a technology. It starts with a problem worth solving.
problema.body: A company can build its own tool to meet an internal need. At this stage, the goal isn't to sell software — it's to make its own process work better.
problema.revealedIntro: That process also reveals things you couldn't see from the outside:
revealedItems: What problem really needs to be solved

darkVirada.body: If other companies face a similar pain point, a solution built internally may have the potential to become a product. That doesn't mean every internal problem will turn into a product — it's a possibility, and every possibility like this needs to be validated.

solucaoProduto.heading: From internal solution to product
solucaoProduto.subheading: You don't need to start big
solucaoProduto.body1: An MVP doesn't need to be a massive platform. It can be a small solution that solves an important part of a specific problem.
solucaoProduto.body2: A company notices, for example, that its customers need to track their requests. Instead of building a complete platform with dozens of features, it can start with:
solucaoProduto.closing: Then, as usage reveals new needs, the product can evolve.

quandoVirarProduto.heading: When a solution can become a product
quandoVirarProduto.intro: A few signals help you see it:
signals: Other companies face the same difficulty
There's a process that can be standardized
There's willingness to pay for the solution
The problem keeps existing even after the first solution

ferramentaSaas.heading: From internal tool to SaaS
ferramentaSaas.body: SaaS can turn a specific solution into a product used continuously by other companies. MicroSaaS is a similar possibility, but for smaller, tightly focused solutions: they solve one specific problem, without trying to do everything.
ferramentaSaas.imageAlt: Four windows in sequence, each more defined than the last, labeled Internal problem, Internal solution, MVP, and Product, representing this evolution

darkSentido.headingPrefix: Before it can be sold, a product needs to
darkSentido.body: Validating the problem and the need comes before investing in a complex platform. The question shouldn't be “what can we build?”.
darkSentido.closing: It should be: which problem is worth solving?

comecarPequeno.heading: Start small
comecarPequeno.body: The product can grow as evidence shows that the solution actually solves a problem.

closing.paragraph2: A tool built to organize your own operation can reveal a process other companies need to solve too.
closing.paragraph3: The first step isn't building a huge platform. It's understanding whether there's a real, recurring problem — relevant enough to become a solution.
closing.heading: Is there a problem your company has already solved internally?
closing.body: The first step can be simple: understanding whether other companies share that same problem.
